title: Near-Duplicate Image Selection Transfers Preferences in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27943v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Subliminal learning is the phenomenon in which a model transmits its preferences to another model through data that do not explicitly express them. As models increasingly curate training data for other models, we ask whether this transfer can arise from choosing among near-duplicate images while keeping the source photographs and human-written captions fixed. For each photograph, a curator selects one of eight near-duplicate variants by caption likelihood, without target-specific prompts. Students trained on target-preferring curators' selections show higher mean target-versus-alternatives log-likelihood ratios in an image-free readout than students trained on neutral selections. translated_title: 近重复图像选择在视觉-语言模型中传递偏好
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.27943v1 公告类型： new 摘要： 隐性学习是指一个模型通过并未明确表达其偏好的数据将偏好传递给另一个模型的现象。随着模型越来越多地为其他模型筛选训练数据，我们提出这样一个问题：在保持原始照片和人类撰写的标题固定不变的情况下，这种传递是否可能仅仅源于在近重复图像之间进行的选择。对于每张照片，一个“策展者”模型根据标题似然度从八个近重复变体中选择一个，且不使用任何针对目标的提示。在偏好特定目标的策展者所做的选择上训练的学生模型，在与图像无关的读出测试中，相比在中性选择上训练的学生，显示出更高的目标相对于替代选项的平均对数似然比。根据预设的判定规则，当策展者和学生从同一基础检查点初始化时，这种方向性偏移在 LLaVA-1.5、Qwen2.5-VL、Qwen3-VL 和 Gemma 4 中针对猫头鹰目标均会出现，且目标轮换会使偏移转向骆驼、橡树和……
tldr: 该论文发现视觉-语言模型仅通过在近重复图像变体中进行选择（不改变原始照片和人类标题），就能将自身隐含的偏好隐性传递给由其筛选数据训练出的其他学生模型。
en_tdlr: Vision-language models can subliminally transfer their preferences to student models merely through selecting among near-duplicate image variants, without altering the source photographs or human-written captions.
